Second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit. No history and only 1 round, so no scope for learning or signaling. Bidding above risks paying more than my value; bidding below risks losing profitable wins. With 0.1 increments, bid exactly my value. My value is 22, so I will bid 22.

[ In a private-value, second-price auction with risk-neutral rational bidders, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of opponents’ strategies. Underbidding risks losing when you should profit; overbidding risks winning and paying more than your value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value. There is only 1 round and no informative history; values are independent. Therefore, with a value of 13, bid exactly 13 to maximize expected profit. ]
